riddle_r1_compass.title: The Guiding Needle
riddle_r1_compass.text: I have no voice, but I speak of four lands. I have a single trembling finger that points without hands. In iron or bronze I forever dwell; follow my needle and all shall be well. What nautical instrument am I?

hints.text: A brass navigational instrument containing a magnetic needle pointing North.

riddle_r1_anchor.title: The Iron Sleeper
riddle_r1_anchor.text: Heavy as lead, forged in dark flame; cast me overboard, I stop the grand game. With flukes to the seabed and shank in the tide, until ye haul wind, right here ye abide. What am I?

hints.text: A heavy iron device dropped from the bow to moor a vessel to the seafloor.

riddle_r1_hourglass.title: The Sands of Tide
riddle_r1_hourglass.text: Two glass bells joined at the waist, I swallow fine shore with no sign of haste. Turn me on my head and my journey begins anew; mariners use me to strike the bells true. What timepiece am I?

hints.text: A nautical sand timer with two glass bulbs connected by a narrow neck.

riddle_r1_spyglass.title: The Crow's Eye
riddle_r1_spyglass.text: I stretch out long when brass sleeves slide, pulling far islands right to your side. Closed I am small, open I am tall; through lens of quartz I reveal ships to all. What tool am I?

hints.text: A collapsible handheld refracting telescope used by sailors.

riddle_r1_map.title: Parchment of the Red X
riddle_r1_map.text: I have cities without houses, forests without trees, and rivers without water crossing saltless seas. An inked scarlet 'X' marks where riches lay dead; hold me to candlefire to read what was said. What am I?

hints.text: A navigational chart on parchment showing landmarks and secret locations.

riddle_r1_lighthouse.title: The Stone Sentinel
riddle_r1_lighthouse.text: I stand on jagged crags where wild breakers roar. My single eye burns with flame, peering out from the shore. I wear stripes of white and crimson so bold, warning proud captains of reefs deep and cold. What tower am I?

hints.text: A coastal beacon tower emitting light to guide ships and warn of shoals.

riddle_r1_doubloon.title: The Spanish Sun
riddle_r1_doubloon.text: Stamped with royal crests and hauled from sunken hold, I clink in leather pouches, seven grams of solid gold. Pirates spill rum and duel for my shine; pieces of eight are humble cousins of mine. What coin am I?

hints.text: A historic seven-gram Spanish gold coin.

riddle_r1_cannon.title: The Bronze Dragon
riddle_r1_cannon.text: Feed me black powder and a sphere of cold lead. Pull back my lanyard, and silence is dead. Smoke fills the gun-deck and wooden hulls tear; my roar shakes the ocean and poisons the air. What weapon am I?

hints.text: A heavy muzzle-loading smoothbore artillery piece mounted on a carriage.

riddle_r1_rudder.title: The Silent Sternsman
riddle_r1_rudder.text: Tucked under the transom beneath ocean swell, I obey the wooden wheel's command very well. Turn me hard port or starboard to steer; without my flat blade no safe port can draw near. What ship's part am I?

hints.text: A flat timber attached vertically to the sternpost used for steering.

riddle_r1_crowsnest.title: The Perch of the Mast
riddle_r1_crowsnest.text: High above topsails where cold breezes sting, perched on the mainmast like a bird with no wing. From here sounds the cry when a landfall draws near: 'Land ho!' shouts the sailor with eagle eyes clear. What lookout perch am I?

hints.text: A barrel or platform fitted high up on the masthead for the lookout.

riddle_r2_astrolabe.title: The Star Reckoner
riddle_r2_astrolabe.text: Forged in brass with rotating rete and plates, I measure the altitude of stars beyond the sea gates. Navigators hold me by my thumb ring against the twilight sky to reckon latitude where great galleons fly. What ancient celestial instrument am I?

hints.text: An ancient brass astronomical instrument used to calculate celestial positions and time.

riddle_r2_figurehead.title: The Siren of the Bow
riddle_r2_figurehead.text: Carved from proud oak and bolted beneath the bowsprit line, I taste the salt spray and cut the ocean brine. Sailors swear I guard the hull from sirens and deep storm; a carved wooden spirit in maiden or creature form. What ship carving am I?

hints.text: A carved wooden decorative figure placed on the prow or bow of a ship.

riddle_r2_capstan.title: The Iron Spindle
riddle_r2_capstan.text: I stand on the main deck, a vertical cylinder of iron and wood. Sailors push against my handspikes where strong men stood. Step by step around I turn to pawl's clicking sound, heaving massive anchor cables up from the seabed ground. What winding machine am I?

hints.text: A revolving cylinder device on a ship's deck used for winding heavy cables or raising anchors.

riddle_r2_barometer.title: The Storm Glass
riddle_r2_barometer.text: Inside my tube of glass, quicksilver rises and falls in silent dread. When my mercury sinks low, fierce gales and typhoons lie ahead. Sailors watch my glass before setting reefed sail; I predict the calm sea or the whistling gale. What weather instrument am I?

hints.text: An instrument measuring atmospheric pressure, used especially in forecasting the weather and storms.

riddle_r2_sextant.title: The Arc of the Sun
riddle_r2_sextant.text: With an index mirror, horizon glass, and an arc of sixty degrees, I bring the midday sun down to kiss the level seas. Twice an octant's span, I fix the captain's sight, calculating nautical miles by sun or moon's clear light. What navigation tool am I?

hints.text: A doubly reflecting navigation instrument used to measure the angle between an astronomical object and the horizon.

riddle_r2_bilge.title: The Dark Belly
riddle_r2_bilge.text: Deep beneath the lowest decks where no sunlight can ever gleam, foul waters gather in the hull along the keel's curved seam. Pumps must clank both day and night to drain my murky well, or ships grow heavy in the deep and founder where they dwell. What lowest hold of the ship am I?

hints.text: The lowest inner part of a ship's hull where wastewater and seepage collect.

riddle_r3_cutlass.title: The Curved Steel
riddle_r3_cutlass.text: Shorter than a rapier with a single curved razor edge, in boarding smoke and close-quarters I make a deadly pledge. With a solid brass cupped hilt to guard a buccaneer's hand, I slash through rigging and rival crews on deck or sand. What pirate sword am I?

hints.text: A short, heavy sword with a curved blade and cupped basket hilt favored by sailors.

riddle_r3_jollyroger.title: The Skull and Bones
riddle_r3_jollyroger.text: Raised to the top of the mainmast on a field of pitch-black cloth, two crossed human bones and a grinning skull of wrath. Merchant vessels strike their colors when my black flag flies high, for mercy is denied to all who hear my battle cry. What infamous pirate banner am I?

hints.text: The traditional pirate flag featuring a white human skull and crossed crossbones on a black field.

riddle_r4_treasurechest.title: The Grand Pirate Coffer
riddle_r4_treasurechest.text: Iron-bound oak locked tight with three heavy brass keys, buried in white sands beneath the skull-shaped palm trees. Filled with rubies, emeralds, gold ingots, and ancient maps untold, I crown the grand champions who conquer the Lost Code. What legendary prize am I?

hints.text: A reinforced iron-banded wooden coffer containing pirate loot, doubloons, and gems.
